<h2 id="about-me-title">About me</h2>
<p>I am an economist and computational researcher studying how economic conditions and power relations shape development, inequality, and political beliefs. My work draws on policy evaluation, experiments, numerical modelling, computational text analysis, and historical institutional analysis. My broader research interests span finance and development, technological change and labour markets, and political and media narratives.</p>
<p>My proposed PhD work asks how currency hierarchy, financing arrangements, and institutional learning shape which public-purpose investments move forward, the state’s capacity to discipline supported capital, the development of productive capabilities, and the distribution of risk and returns. I am developing two empirical pilots: one compares successive generations of public-private partnership contracts in Chile, while the other examines energy-project finance in Malawi.</p>
